notes: compose:name carries the whole-project raw/structured outputs (compose_yaml, project, content_sha256) because it is the facet that IS the project (its name/id); compose:cli-config (docker_compose_config) repeats them for the read-only render. Every other docker_compose facet (services, networks, volumes, configs, secrets, models, jobs, include) declares the SAME `project` attribute restricted to its slice, plus no_raw_reason pointing at compose:name.

Pointers: both schema files use JSON Schema 2020-12 `$defs`, not `definitions`; pointers are written `#/$defs/...` (e.g. #/$defs/container_spec/properties/image). A service's direct properties are the union of $defs/container_spec, $defs/workload_spec and $defs/service (allOf); each field points at the def that declares it. Field pointers are into compose-spec.json; the same JSON path exists in compose-go-embedded.json for every field except jobs.*.extends.

Schema differences (compose-spec @ 3a4a699 vs compose-go v2.16.2 embedded): (1) container_spec mem_limit, memswap_limit, shm_size are integer|string in compose-spec and number|string in compose-go. Those fields carry schema=compose-go-embedded (the provider validates with compose-go); the TF type is number either way after normalization (bytes). build.shm_size is integer|string in BOTH files and is not affected. (2) jobs.*.extends exists only in compose-spec; the field carries schema=compose-spec and the compose:jobs project slice follows compose-spec (output schema=compose-spec), all other project outputs (compose:name, compose:cli-config, every other facet, build, deploy) follow compose-go-embedded.

Normalized-form typing: the structured fields mirror the NORMALIZED project (what `docker compose config` prints), so oneOf short/long forms are typed by their long form: list_or_dict -> map(string) (environment, labels, annotations, sysctls, build.args), string_or_list/command -> list(string), build/extends/include/ports/volumes/secrets/configs entries -> object, depends_on/service networks/service models -> map(object), ulimits -> map(object{soft,hard}), extra_hosts -> map(list(string)), boolean|string -> bool, integer/number|string -> number, external (bool|string|object) -> bool, umask -> string.

Depth: `project` lists every top-level property (version, name, include, services, models, networks, volumes, secrets, configs, jobs); every direct property of a service (and of a job); build, deploy, healthcheck, ports and volumes (long syntax) one more level, and the direct properties of network/volume/secret/config/model/include definitions. Deeper levels (deploy.resources.*, deploy.placement.*, volumes[].bind.*, blkio_config.*, develop.watch[] ...) are left to the mechanical rule: fields_complete=false.

Sensitivity: compose_yaml and project are sensitive as a whole, because environment, env_file, build.args/secrets/ssh, configs.content, secrets sources and ANY interpolated ${VAR} can carry a secret. Fields that are the usual carriers have an extra field-level `sensitive: true` annotation (informational). content_sha256 of a sensitive raw is not marked sensitive. Logs (logs_json/entries), top (process args), ps (Command) and exec/run stdout/stderr are sensitive; this is stricter than today's data.docker_logs (not sensitive) and matches docker_exec_output (sensitive).

Actions: there is no raw/structured requirement; `result`/`results` objects (exec, run, wait) are structured with fields, everything else is identity (IDs/refs changed or returned). known_after_apply is true for every action output.

known_after_apply: compose_yaml/project/hash/image_refs are false because docker_compose parses the project at plan time (spec_hash is computed in plan); IDs created by the Engine are true. Version pins (compose_spec_version, compose_go_version) are build-time constants (false); engine versions are true on resources/actions and false on data sources.
Field annotations beyond SCHEMA.md: `schema`, `schema_note`, `sensitive`, `note` on FIELD and `schema` on OUTPUT, as the lane brief asked; merge.py does not check FIELD keys.

compose:service-build and compose:service-deploy are proposed under docker_image / docker_service (inventory names); their outputs here are only the compose-facing slice (`build`, `deploy` objects + identity), not those resources' Engine inspect outputs, which other lanes own.

compose:cli-ls fields (Name, Status, ConfigFiles) come from `docker compose ls --format json`; compose_ls.md documents the json format but not the keys, so the keys are from compose's output and pointed at the labels they derive from.
naming_questions: docker_compose exposes the project name as `id` and `project_name`; the contract's identity name is `name`. Add a `name` alias, rename project_name to name (breaking), or keep project_name?

Facets of docker_compose: one `project` attribute (whole project) as proposed, or per-slice attributes (`project_services`, `project_networks`, ...) that do not clash with today's computed `services`/`networks`/`volumes` ID maps?
docker_compose_logs raw output: `logs_json` (JSON array of entries, as proposed) or a plain-text `logs` / `output` string like `docker compose logs` prints?
Action results: `result` object {exit_code, stdout, stderr} (as proposed for docker_compose_exec / _run) or flat `exit_code` / `stdout` / `stderr` like docker_exec_output?
